What’s New in Version 5.1
 Virtual Stop-Loss / Take-Profit: all trailing can now be handled internally by the EA and 
executed with market orders, instead of modifying orders at the broker.
 Two new news filters: Interest Rate (central bank rate decisions) and CPI (inflation). Both are 
off by default.
 Trade Frequency: when a strategy is switched off, its pending orders are now removed 
automatically. Any trades that strategy still has open continue to be managed normally until 
they close.
 The information panel now shows the correct profit and loss per strategy, including trades 
taken before this update.
 Fixed trade management on brokers whose trading session crosses midnight. On those 
brokers, trailing and other management could previously pause for most of the day.
 The information panel has been restyled to match our other EAs.

2. Key Features
 Extremely easy setup – attach to chart, set your Max Allowed Drawdown, and start trading
 Up to 9 internal strategies with Trade Frequency (Auto) or full manual selection
 Fully automated lot sizing with Weighted Lotsize and multiple calculation methods
 Variable Values that automatically adapt to the current Gold price
 Built-in NFP news filter with MQL5 Calendar and AutoGMT support
 Prop-firm ready with daily drawdown protection and unique trade settings
 Advanced trailing including HL_TrailingSL and Fake Breakout Filter
 Real-time information panel on the chart
 Regular free updates and dedicated support from Profalgo LTD

6. Quick Start Setup (Recommended by Profalgo LTD)
1. Attach the EA to an XAUUSD H1 chart.
2. Set TradeFrequency to Auto (based on balance and risk) (recommended for most users).
3. Set Lotsize calculation method to Max Allowed Total Drawdown.
4. Set Max Allowed TOTAL Drawdown to your preferred risk level (e.g. 10–30%).
5. Enable Weighted Lotsize = true.
6. Enable UseVariableValues = true and AdjustLotsizeToVariableValues = true.
7. Set EnableNFP_Filter = true and UseMQL5Calendar = true.
8. Leave Fake Breakout Filter on Medium and UseHL_TrailingSL = true.
For Prop-Firm Accounts: Use our dedicated Prop Firm set file, enable Set Max DAILY Drawdown, set 
Randomization higher, and adjust the Prop Firm Unique Trade Settings.
7. Input Parameters – Full Explanation
General Settings
 UseVariableValues – Gold has roughly doubled in price over the years, which means a fixed 
stop-loss or entry distance no longer means the same thing it did when the strategies were 
developed. With this enabled, the EA scales every entry, stop-loss, take-profit and trailing 
distance in proportion to the current Gold price, so the strategies keep behaving the same 
way as the market moves. We strongly recommend leaving this on, for live trading and for 
backtests alike – turning it off makes older backtest periods look very different from recent 
ones. (default: true)
 AdjustLotsizeToVariableValues – Works together with UseVariableValues. When the scaling 
widens the stop-loss distance, the same lot size would risk more money than intended, so 
this reduces the lot size to compensate (and increases it again when distances shrink). Leave 
it on whenever UseVariableValues is on, otherwise your real risk per trade drifts as the Gold 
price changes. (default: true)
 ShowInfoPanel – Shows the live information panel on the chart: account and balance 
figures, the lot sizes in use, and the profit and loss of each individual strategy. Turn it off only 
if you run many charts on a weak VPS and want to save a little processing time. (default: 
true)
 Update infopanel during testing – Draws and updates the information panel during Strategy 
Tester runs. It makes backtests noticeably slower, so it is off by default. Enable it only when 
you actually want to watch the panel while a test is running. (default: false)
 Adjustment for Infopanel size – Scales the whole information panel up or down. Increase it 
above 1.0 on high-resolution or 4K monitors where the panel looks too small, or decrease it 
below 1.0 if the panel takes up too much of the chart. (default: 1)
 Force Font Size (0=disabled) – Forces a specific font size for the information panel instead of 
letting the EA choose one from your screen resolution. Leave it at 0 unless the automatically 
chosen size does not suit your setup. (default: 0)

 Backtest Speed – Speeds up Strategy Tester runs by having the EA process fewer price 
updates per bar. This affects the Strategy Tester only and has no effect whatsoever on live 
trading. Use the faster settings for quick exploratory runs, then confirm your final results on 
normal, which is the most accurate. Options: normal, fast, ultra fast. (default: normal)
Trading Settings
 Allow Buy Trades – Allows the EA to open long positions. Switching this off stops new buy 
trades being opened but does not close or abandon any buy trade that is already running – 
those continue to be managed normally until they close. (default: true)
 Allow Sell Trades – Allows the EA to open short positions. As with buy trades, switching it off 
only stops new sell entries; anything already open continues to be managed until it closes. 
(default: true)
 TradeFrequency – Controls how many of the internal strategies run at the same time, and 
therefore how often the EA trades and how much risk it takes. Auto is the recommended 
setting: the EA picks a sensible number of strategies for your balance and your chosen 
maximum drawdown, and adjusts as the account grows. The fixed levels let you override that 
choice, and Manual strategy selection hands you the individual switches further down. When 
a strategy is switched off, any pending orders it had are removed automatically, while any 
trade it already has open keeps being managed until it closes. Options: extreme 
conservative, conservative, moderate, Intense, Extreme (high risk!), Auto (based on balance 
and risk), Manual strategy selection. (default: Auto (based on balance and risk))
 Max Allowed Spread – The widest spread, in points, at which the EA will still place new 
orders. Above it, entries are held back until the spread comes in again, which protects you 
during news spikes and thin market hours. It does not prevent existing trades from being 
managed or closed. Note that this value is also scaled by UseVariableValues, so it keeps pace 
with the Gold price. (default: 500.0)
 UseHL_TrailingSL – Enables the advanced High-Low trailing stop, which trails the stop behind 
recent swing highs and lows rather than at a fixed distance from price. It tends to give trends 
more room while still protecting profit. Only the strategies that are configured to use it are 
affected. (default: true)
 Friday stop hour (brokertime; close all trades) – The hour of the broker's clock on Friday at 
which the EA stops opening trades and closes everything still open, so nothing is carried over 
the weekend. Set it to 25 (or any value above 23) to disable the behaviour entirely and let 
trades run into the close. (default: 25)
 SetSL_TP_After_Entry – A compatibility option for brokers that refuse pending orders which 
already carry a stop-loss and take-profit. When enabled, the EA sends the pending order 
without them and attaches both as soon as the order is filled. Leave it off unless your broker 
actually rejects orders, because it means there is a very brief moment after the fill before the 
stop is in place. (default: false)
 Use Virtual Expiration – Some brokers do not accept an expiry time on pending orders. With 
this enabled the EA does not ask the broker to expire them at all, and instead deletes them 
itself once they are old enough. The practical effect is the same, and it works on every 
broker, which is why it is on by default. (default: true)
 Randomization (entries and exit in pips) – Shifts entries, stops and targets by a small 
random amount, in pips, on every trade. It exists for prop-firm accounts: if you run the same 
EA on several accounts, identical trades across them can be flagged as copy trading. A value

around 50 is a sensible starting point for prop firms. Leave it at 0 on a normal account, where 
it only adds noise. (default: 0)
 Fake Breakout Filter – Protection against false breakouts. After a trade opens, the EA checks 
whether the candle it entered on actually closed in the trade's favour; if that candle closed 
against the position, the trade is closed straight away rather than being left to run to its full 
stop-loss. The stronger settings apply the same check on more timeframes, which cuts losses 
sooner but also closes some trades that would have recovered. Options: OFF, Low, Medium, 
High. (default: Medium)
 Base Magicnumber – The starting magic number the EA uses to tag its trades, so it can tell 
its own positions apart from everything else on the account. Each internal strategy gets its 
own number counting up from this one. Only change it if you run two copies of this same EA 
on one account, and then give each copy a base number far enough apart that the ranges 
cannot overlap. (default: 8000)
 Comment for trades – The comment attached to every trade the EA opens, which is what 
you see in your terminal and account history. Change it freely; it has no effect on trading. 
 RemoveCommentSuffix – By default the EA appends the strategy identifier to each trade 
comment, so you can see which strategy opened which trade. Enable this to strip that suffix 
and leave only your own comment text, which some prop firms and copy services prefer. 
(default: false)
 License Key (for non MQL5 version) – Your licence key. This is only needed if you did not buy 
through MQL5.com -- for MQL5.com purchases the licence is handled automatically and this 
field stays empty. (default: empty)
News Filter (NFP)
 EnableNFP_Filter – Switches on the Non-Farm Payroll filter. NFP is the single most volatile 
scheduled event for Gold, with violent spikes in both directions and very wide spreads, so by 
default the EA steps aside around it. The two settings below control whether it closes open 
trades, deletes pending orders, or both. (default: true)
 UseMQL5Calendar – Takes the exact release time from the economic calendar built into MT5 
rather than from the EA's internal table of dates. This is the more accurate option and we 
recommend leaving it on. It needs the MT5 calendar to be populated – on a fresh VPS, open 
Toolbox, Calendar once and let it sync. In the Strategy Tester the calendar is not available, so 
the EA automatically falls back to its internal dates. (default: true)
 AutoGMT – Works out your broker's GMT offset automatically, which is what the news filter 
needs in order to convert release times into your broker's clock. Leave it on for live trading. 
The two manual offsets below are used only when this is off, or when backtesting. (default: 
true)
 GMT_OFFSET_Winter – Your broker's GMT offset during winter time, used when AutoGMT is 
off or when backtesting. Getting this wrong shifts the news windows by whole hours, so 
check it against your broker's stated server time rather than guessing. (default: 2)
 GMT_OFFSET_Summer – Your broker's GMT offset during summer (daylight saving) time, 
used when AutoGMT is off or when backtesting. Most brokers move their clock by one hour 
in summer, so this is usually the winter value plus one. (default: 3)
(default: bot‐cua‐toi‐3)

 NFP_CloseOpenTrades – Closes any open trades before the NFP release. Switch it off if you 
would rather let running trades take their chances through the news and only stop new 
orders being placed. (default: true)
 NFP_ClosePendingOrders – Deletes resting pending orders before the NFP release, so a spike 
cannot trigger an entry in the middle of the chaos. The EA places fresh orders again once the 
window has passed. (default: true)
 NFP_MinutesBefore – How many minutes before the release the filter starts. Increase it if 
your broker's spread begins widening well ahead of the announcement. (default: 100)
 NFP_MinutesAfter – How many minutes after the release the EA waits before trading again. 
Increase it if you want to sit out the whipsaw that often follows the first reaction. (default: 
60)
Interest Rate Filter
The Interest Rate and CPI filters work the same way as the NFP filter and can be used alongside it. 
Both are switched off by default, so nothing changes unless you enable them.
 EnableIR_Filter – Switches on the interest-rate filter, which covers scheduled central bank 
rate decisions. These move Gold sharply and are worth avoiding for the same reasons as NFP . 
It is off by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it on, and it can be used alongside the 
NFP and CPI filters. (default: false)
 IR_CloseOpenTrades – Closes open trades before the rate decision. Switch it off to leave 
running trades alone and only block new entries. (default: true)
 IR_ClosePendingOrders – Deletes resting pending orders before the rate decision, so the 
spike cannot trigger an entry. Fresh orders are placed again afterwards. (default: true)
 IR_MinutesBefore – How many minutes before the rate decision the filter starts. (default: 
100)
 IR_MinutesAfter – How many minutes after the rate decision the EA waits before trading 
again. Rate decisions are often followed by a press conference that moves the market a 
second time, so a longer window than usual can be sensible here. (default: 60)
CPI Filter
 EnableCPI_Filter – Switches on the CPI (inflation) filter. CPI releases are one of the main 
drivers of Gold and routinely cause large, fast moves. It is off by default, and can be used 
alongside the NFP and interest-rate filters. (default: false)
 CPI_CloseOpenTrades – Closes open trades before the CPI release. Switch it off to leave 
running trades alone and only block new entries. (default: true)
 CPI_ClosePendingOrders – Deletes resting pending orders before the CPI release, so the 
spike cannot trigger an entry. Fresh orders are placed again afterwards. (default: true)
 CPI_MinutesBefore – How many minutes before the CPI release the filter starts. (default: 
100)
 CPI_MinutesAfter – How many minutes after the CPI release the EA waits before trading 
again. (default: 60)
Virtual Stop-Loss / Take-Profit

By default the EA places a real Stop-Loss and Take-Profit on the server and moves them as the trade 
develops. With Virtual SL/TP enabled, the initial Stop-Loss and Take-Profit are still placed on the 
server exactly as before, but every later adjustment is kept internally by the EA and executed with a 
market order instead. Your trade is therefore never unprotected. This is useful on brokers with wide 
stop levels, or where frequent order modifications are discouraged.
 Enable Virtual SL/TP (trailing by market close) – Changes how the EA moves your stop and 
target once a trade is running. Normally every adjustment is sent to the broker as an order 
modification. With this enabled the EA keeps the moving levels in its own memory instead 
and closes the trade with a market order when one is reached. The original stop-loss and 
take-profit are still placed on the server exactly as before, so the trade is never unprotected. 
This helps on brokers with wide minimum stop distances, or where constant order 
modifications are discouraged. The trade-off is that the EA must be running and connected 
for the virtual levels to be acted on. (default: false)
 Seconds before the real SL is pulled up to the virtual SL – Only applies when Virtual SL/TP is 
enabled. It sets how long the EA waits before also pulling the real stop-loss at the broker up 
to the virtual level, which gives you server-side protection even if your VPS goes down. Set it 
to 0 to keep the exit completely virtual, in which case the real stop-loss is never moved from 
where it started and the trade is always closed by market order unless that original stop is 
hit. (default: 99)
Prop Firm Unique Trade Settings
 AdjustEntry – Shifts every entry price by this many pips. Together with the other 
adjustments below, it exists so that the same EA running on several prop-firm accounts does 
not place identical trades, which can be flagged as copy trading. Leave it at 0 on a normal 
account. (default: 0)
 AdjustSL – Shifts every stop-loss by this many pips. A positive value widens the stop and 
therefore increases the risk per trade, so change it in small steps and remember that your lot 
sizing is based on the original distance. (default: 0)
 AdjustTP – Shifts every take-profit by this many pips, making targets slightly nearer or 
further away than standard. (default: 0)
 AdjustTrailSL – Shifts the trailing stop distance by this many pips, so the trail sits a little 
tighter or looser than standard. (default: 0)
 AdjustTrailTP – Shifts the trailing take-profit distance by this many pips. (default: 0)
 AdjustBreakEven – Shifts the break-even level by this many pips, changing how much profit 
is locked in when the trade reaches break-even. (default: 0)

Lot Size Settings
 Manually set balance to use (if > 0) – Makes the EA size its trades from a fixed balance 
figure instead of your real account balance. Useful when you want to trade only part of an 
account, or to keep lot sizes steady while you add or withdraw funds. Leave it at 0 to use the 
real balance. (default: 0)
 Lotsize calculation method – Chooses how the EA works out its lot sizes. This is the most 
important setting in this section, because it decides which of the values below actually does 
anything – the others are ignored. Options: use StartLots, Max Allowed Total Drawdown, 
Max Risk Per Strategy. (default: Max Allowed Total Drawdown)
 StartLots – The fixed lot size used when the lot size calculation method is set to the manual 
option. It is ignored by every other method. Note this is the lot size per strategy, not for the 
account as a whole, so the total exposure depends on how many strategies are running. 
(default: 0.01)
 Max Allowed TOTAL Drawdown – Your main risk control. You tell the EA the largest total 
drawdown you are prepared to accept, as a percentage of the balance, and it sizes every 
strategy so that the historical worst case stays within that figure. Lower values mean smaller 
lots and a smoother curve; higher values mean bigger lots and bigger swings. Something in 
the 10 to 30 percent range suits most traders. It only applies when the lot size calculation 
method is set to Max Allowed Total Drawdown. (default: 30)
 Weighted Lotsize – Spreads the risk evenly across the strategies that are running, instead of 
giving each one the same lot size. Because the strategies have different historical 
drawdowns, equal lot sizes would mean the riskier ones dominate the account. We 
recommend leaving this on. (default: true)
 Max Risk Per Strat – The maximum risk, as a percentage, allotted to each individual strategy. 
It applies when the lot size calculation method is set to Max Risk Per Strategy. Because every 
running strategy gets this allowance, your total exposure is roughly this figure multiplied by 
the number of active strategies – so raise it in small steps. (default: 1)
 Set Max DAILY Drawdown (Prop Firms) – A hard daily loss limit, as a percentage. If the 
account loses this much in a single day the EA closes everything and stops trading until the 
next day. It exists for prop-firm rules that fail an account on daily loss. Set it a little tighter 
than the firm's actual limit so that spread and slippage cannot push you past the line. 0 
disables it. (default: 0)
 OnlyUp – Stops lot sizes from shrinking after losses. The EA remembers the highest balance 
the account has reached and keeps sizing from that figure, so a drawdown does not also cut 
your position sizes and slow the recovery. The trade-off is that risk stays at the higher level 
while the account is down, so it is more aggressive than letting lots fall away. (default: true)
 CheckMargin – Checks that enough free margin is available before sending an order, and 
skips the trade if not. Leave it on – it prevents rejected orders and margin warnings on 
smaller accounts. (default: true)
 Use Equity Instead of Balance – Sizes trades from account equity rather than balance, which 
means open floating profit or loss is taken into account. This makes the EA reduce size while 
trades are under water and increase it while they are in profit, which is a more conservative 
approach but also a more variable one. (default: false)

 Reset Highest Balance for OnlyUp – Clears the highest-balance figure that OnlyUp 
remembers, so lot sizing starts again from your current balance. Use it after a withdrawal, or 
if you want the EA to trade smaller following a drawdown. Enable it, let the EA run for one 
tick, then set it back to false. (default: false)
Manual Strategy Selection
Important Note: Do NOT use manual strategy selection while using the “Max Allowed Total 
Drawdown” option!
 Run Strategy 1 (low risk) – Switches individual strategies on and off by hand. These only take 
effect when Trade Frequency is set to Manual strategy selection; otherwise the EA decides 
for itself and these are ignored. Lower-numbered strategies are the lower-risk ones. Do not 
combine manual selection with the Max Allowed Total Drawdown sizing method, because 
that method needs to know which strategies are running in order to size them correctly. 
(default: true)
8. Recommended Risk Management
We strongly recommend using TradeFrequency = Auto and Lotsize calculation method = Max 
Allowed Total Drawdown. Keep Weighted Lotsize = true, UseVariableValues = true, and 
AdjustLotsizeToVariableValues = true for best performance. 
For prop firms, enable Set Max DAILY Drawdown and use higher Randomization.
9. Backtesting Recommendations
 Test on XAUUSD H1 chart
 Test with “1Minute OHLC” mode on your broker’s data, or real ticks for most secure tests
 Keep UseVariableValues = true and AdjustLotsizeToVariableValues = true for realistic long-
term results
 Always verify results on a demo account before going live
